transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I can’t get rid of this feeling that I’ve failed as a father, and really as a useful person. It just keeps going around in my head, and I end up feeling like I don’t deserve much of a future.
About how long have you been feeling this way?
About a month now—since my daughter left for college out of state.
Have you ever experienced a period like this in the past where you felt this depressed or overwhelmed?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of another time it’s felt this bad or this overwhelming.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in doing things you normally enjoy?
Yeah. I used to look forward to working on my model railway, and watching Cubs games with my daughter. Now the trains are just sitting there half-built, and even turning on a game feels pointless.
How has your sleep been over this past month?

It’s been pretty bad. I lie awake for hours because the house is so quiet, and then I wake up around three or four in the morning. Once I’m up, my mind just goes over everything I’ve messed up, and I can’t get back to sleep.
How have your energy levels been during the day?
My energy is really low. Even simple things, like carrying laundry upstairs or sorting the mail, feel like I’m moving through wet cement, no matter how long I’ve been in bed.
With feeling like you don't deserve much of a future, have you had any thoughts of wanting to end your life or hurting yourself?
I've had thoughts that it might be easier if I just didn't wake up. That scares me. I caught myself going over my finances like I was getting things ready for somebody else.
